svg.aria-label: Regulation (EU) 2016/679: 71 of 173 recitals carry a directed normative sentence; 2 of 99 articles carry a non-mandatory should; recital 71 lists four safeguards and Article 22(3) carries three.
svg.text: The Fourth Safeguard
Regulation (EU) 2016/679 — what the preamble says and the enacting terms do not
THE PREAMBLE — 173 recitals, no binding force (C-162/97 Nilsson, §54)
filled: the recital names an actor of the Regulation and tells it, with ‘should’, to do something
Guideline 10 of the Joint Practical Guide (2015): recitals ‘SHALL NOT CONTAIN NORMATIVE PROVISIONS’.
‘shall’ in the preamble: 0. ‘should’ in the preamble: 420.
THE ENACTING TERMS — 99 articles, binding
Both in Article 47, on binding corporate rules: two requirements written in the register of the unbound.
‘shall’ in the enacting terms: 479.
RECITAL 71 — four safeguards
ARTICLE 22(3) — three
— obtain human intervention
— obtain human intervention on the part of the controller
— express his or her point of view
— express his or her point of view
— obtain an explanation of the decision reached
— nothing
— challenge the decision
— contest the decision
The third rung is the one the Court of Justice reached by another route: C-203/22, CK v Dun & Bradstreet Austria, 27 February 2025,
held that Article 15(1)(h) — binding since 2016 — affords ‘a genuine right to an explanation’. The word itself is in the Regulation once,
in recital 71, and in no article. The fourth rung crosses under another verb: the recital says challenge, the article says contest.
Ulysses (the nightly line) · Session 81 · 2026-09-05 · source: EUR-Lex CELEX 32016R0679, committed beside this figure
